evidence: Closed-form hand calculations (calc_hardware.py → calc_out.json) with catalogue numbers (sources below) and coefficients marked ASSUMED. Nothing designed in CAD, built, bench-tested or flown. Not physical verification; M-070 not_run, G-MATURE closed. No purchasing; cost classes are order-of-magnitude.
headline: Recommended: architecture A+ — reel in a lumbar back unit (hip-pack form) with a hinged 0.55 m "scorpion quiver" that is the dock, the launch rail and the line exit; flyer = 111 g (with 15 % margin) folding "umbrella delta" that is folded passively by being pulled nose-first into the quiver trumpet.

The line-exit position, not the reel, is the design driver: any exit on the upper back/shoulder or on a mast gives ≤0.34 m head clearance (calc: shoulder 0.07–0.34 m, 0.6 m mast 0.25 m). A lumbar exit 0.55 m behind the pivot gives ≥1.0 m up to 55° line elevation; 0.65 m gives it up to 65°.

High L/D makes the line steep (70–80° with an un-braked delta/glider) — this solves the clothesline (line ≥1.85 m above snow 1 m behind at 45°) but breaks head clearance above ≈55°, so the flyer needs an elevation (drag/AoA) control, not more L/D. Target band 40–55°.

B (reel on flyer) fails on kinetic energy: +72 g of reel/driver/cell → ≈0.20 kg flyer → 12.2 m/s KE cap, below normal rider speed. C (spring) cannot store a full retract (25 m × 2 N ≈ 50 J ≈ 150–400 g of spring steel); keep it only as a short-stroke dancer for slack take-up.

Reel: T-Motor MN3110 700 Kv + 2:1 GT2 belt + 4 mm-wide "yo-yo" drum (r 15→22 mm, no level-wind) on a 4S1P Molicel P28A pack: all operating points feasible at −10 °C with ≤5.7 C peak (vs kite2 15.8 C). Hold/limit by ratchet + slip clutch at 35 N, not by the motor.

Every slender part sized by hand calc: quiver 56×0.6 mm carbon σ 11.5 MPa at 35 N lateral; delta LE spars 5×4 mm σ 97 MPa/7 mm sag (3×2 mm would be 331 MPa/42 mm — the "3 mm boom" trap, rejected); struts 3–4 mm SF 7.6–21 in Euler; kite2 3 mm boom reproduced (3353 mm tip deflection, 933 MPa) for contrast.

requirements_used.reelInSpeed_ms: ≤6 (retract), ≤3 m/s at 15 N (pumping), 5 m/s at 20 N (tailwind bursts)
requirements_used.payoutSpeed_ms: ≤9 m/s at full drum (above that BEMF > cold bus voltage → uncontrolled diode regen)

A_backReel.summary: Motor, drum, sensors, battery and dock on the body; only the wing + camera fly.
pros: big motor/battery allowed (worn mass rule 1.5 kg)
battery kept warm by the body
line angle + tension measured at the anchor (Fotokite-style state estimation)
retract works even if the flyer electronics die
cons: line always runs from the body → exit geometry vs head/clothesline
dock must be on the body and survive falls/chairlift
A_backReel.verdict: recommended (with a short-stroke dancer from C)

B_reelOnFlyer.summary: Drum and motor on the flyer, line anchored at the body.

calc.note: KE cap below typical rider speed 12-15 m/s before any swing about the rider -> fails KE

cons: reel-in work (T·v up to 100 W) drawn from a flyer cell in the cold
line still anchored to the body → same head/clothesline geometry, no gain
spinning drum + line spooling on a 100 g camera platform → jitter

C_hybrid_springBack.summary: Small fast motor reel + passive constant-force spring.
C_hybrid_springBack.calc: full-retract spring energy ≈ 2 N × 25 m = 50 J; spring steel σ²/2E ≈ 0.7 J/g ideal, 0.1–0.3 J/g practical → 170–500 g (ASSUMED practical factor)
C_hybrid_springBack.useful_part: a 0.3 m dancer arm (doubles to 0.6 m line accumulator) with a 1–2 N spring: sub-10 ms slack take-up at stops/heave and a passive tension floor when the motor driver trips; +15–20 g
C_hybrid_springBack.verdict: only as a dancer inside A

line.choice: 8-carrier UHMWPE (Dyneema/Spectra) braid 0.36 mm, 50 lb class (≈222 N), PU-coated, hi-vis; 25 m on the drum (first 0.5 m at the flyer: 0.6 mm sleeve for abrasion at the nose probe)

checks.note: snap-back: the stored energy goes into ~2-3 g of line; aerodynamic drag of a 0.36 mm line limits recoil speed, but the free end can whip; weak link + cutter decide where it parts

line.drag: cross-flow drag of 15 m at 15 m/s ≈ 0.5·1.0·225·0.36e-3·15·1.1 = 0.67 N (≈half acts at the flyer) — 7 % of a 10 N flight tension; 0.6 mm conductive line would be 1.1 N
line.cold_UV_abrasion: UHMWPE keeps strength in cold (no glass transition in the ski range) and is UV-resistant per Dyneema/Marlow; creep negligible at ≤25 N on a 222 N line; abrasion: SiC/ceramic guides only, never aluminium (ASSUMED good practice). Ice: braid absorbs water and can freeze to the drum → PU coating + wipe at the mouth.
line.conductive_tether: NOT recommended for baseline: a 4–10 k rpm drum needs a slip ring (capsule rings are rated a few hundred rpm — ASSUMED typical) or an inductive rotary transformer; conductor fatigue on a 30 mm drum; 3.6× line weight. Alternative used: 1S 450 mAh flyer cell topped up through dock pogo contacts on every lift ride (cell warmed to >5 °C before charge).
line.cut_hazard: a 0.36 mm line under 10–25 N is a laceration hazard for third parties; line height ≥1.8 m 1 m behind at ε≥45° reduces but does not remove it (resort permission gate as round 4).

motor.source: https://www.getfpv.com/tiger-motor-mn3110-17-700kv.html ; https://www.ligpower.com/product/mn3110-kv700-motor-navigator-type.html (700 Kv, 92 mΩ, 80 g bare / 99 g with leads, 21 A/180 s)
motor.why: low-Kv 37 mm outrunner: enough torque for 25 N hold at 2:1 with ≤22 A, and 6 m/s on a 15 mm drum radius at 12.4 V cold bus; backdrivable (good for tension control, no gearbox stiction)

reel.transmission: 2:1 GT2 6 mm belt (20T/40T), effective belt tension 60 N at the 35 N clutch limit (Gates allowable working tension ASSUMED ≥100 N)

drum.type: "yo-yo" narrow drum, 4 mm gap — no level-wind (the line self-stacks; effective radius tracked from the metering wheel). Solid 6061 hub; hub pressure 54.0 MPa at 15 N wind-on (spool-burst mode for braid: wind on at ≤5 N → 18 MPa).

driver.part: mjbots moteus r4.11 (FOC, encoder, CAN-FD, 10–44 V, 100 A peak phase, 14.2 g)
driver.source: https://github.com/mjbots/moteus (r4.11: 10–44 V, 100 A peak phase, 14.2 g; c1: 10–51 V, 20 A peak, 100 W, 8.9 g) ; https://hackaday.io/project/179234-moteus-brushless-controller
rejected: moteus-c1 100 W peak (pumping bursts need 140 W)
FPV AM32 ESC (no true torque control at stall)

brake_clutch_cut: Mechanical slip clutch (wave-spring friction, line-equivalent 35 N) between drum and pulley: the body-force limit holds with the electronics dead.
Power-off ratchet pawl (spring-engaged, solenoid-released): holds the line when power fails or while docked; reel-in still possible (ratchet direction).

Pay-out braking energy (25 N × 10 m/s × 2 s = 500 J) goes to a 10 W shunt resistor/short-circuit braking unless the pack thermistor reads >5 °C (cold Li-ion must not be charged — components.js chargeBelow0C=false). Dumped in the windings it is +14 K on the motor.

Emergency cut: spring-loaded ceramic guillotine at the drum exit released by a micro solenoid latch (<50 ms, ASSUMED); manual pull-handle on the shoulder strap; weak link 60–80 N at the drum anchor. Nichrome burn-wire rejected as the primary cut (1.6 A for 5–10 s in NRL practice — too slow).
KE governor: reel-in speed limited in software to keep |v_rider + v_reel·ê| ≤ √(2·14.9/m) − 1 m/s; at 12 m/s rider and ε 45° that is ≤4.6 m/s.

sensing.tension: custom aluminium flexure under the middle roller of a 3-roller metering head (full strain bridge) read by a TI ADS1220 (−40…125 °C) + motor current as a cross-check. TE FX29 rejected: rated 0…50 °C only.
sensing.length: idler wheel Ø20 mm with AS5600 magnetic encoder (independent of yo-yo radius); drum encoder from the moteus.
sensing.lineAngle: 2-axis gimballed exit eyelet at the trumpet with two AS5600 (−40…125 °C); fused with the back-unit IMU → line direction in the world frame (Fotokite-style taut-tether estimation).
sources: https://dblp.uni-trier.de/pid/31/5374.html (Lupashin & D'Andrea, IROS 2013, taut-tether inertial sensing) ; https://robohub.org/robots-fotokite-phi (tether direction from tension = position)

battery.peakCrate_note: peak ~10-13 A from a 2.8 Ah cell = 3.6-4.6 C vs 35 A (12.5 C) rating at 25 C; kite2 needed 15.8 C from a 12 Wh 3S LiPo at -10 C (A4-K2-07)
battery.choice: 4S1P Molicel P28A (18650, 2.8 Ah, 35 A) in the insulated back unit against the body; 10 W shunt for pay-out; flyer: 1S 450 mAh LiPo (≈11 g) charged in the dock only above +5 °C cell temperature

dock_launch_capture.concept: "Scorpion quiver": a 56 mm × 0.47 m carbon tube + 0.08 m trumpet, hinged at the right lumbar pivot with a hollow hinge pin that carries the line along the hinge axis (deploy rotation does not change line length).
dock_launch_capture.skiing_stowed: stowed diagonally across the back (right hip → left shoulder blade, ≈35° from vertical) in a shallow channel of a slim back plate; outer thickness ≈65 mm (like a 10–15 L ski pack). The flyer's tail carries a disc that plugs the mouth (snow/ice seal).
dock_launch_capture.chairlift: mechanical lockout pin + software lockout (barometric/GNSS ascent at lift speed, seated posture from IMU, lift-line geofence). Launching on a lift = line into the haul rope → catastrophic; this lockout is safety-critical and must be two-channel. Sitting against the backrest with a 65 mm plate is ASSUMED acceptable (user test needed).
dock_launch_capture.deploy: fold drive (Pololu 1000:1 HPCB + 3:1 spur, stall 2.9 N·m, need 1.4 N·m) swings the quiver to the flight position (pointing rearward, −10° pitch) in ≈1.3 s; detent with breakaway (≤60 N at the tip in any direction except along the line).
dock_launch_capture.launch: Flyer sits nose-first toward the reel, tail at the mouth → it is already oriented nose-into-the-apparent-wind. Ratchet released, motor pays out at ~1–2 m/s; a 0.15 m spring plunger pushes the tail out of the body wake; the umbrella runner spring opens the wings; tension builds, pay-out speeds up to the target length. Launch gate: estimated apparent wind ≥7.4 m/s (needed for ε 45° and ≥1.5 N measurable tension, calc) — below that, stay docked.
dock_launch_capture.capture: Stop/command → KE-governed reel-in, flyer trimmed to high AoA (low elevation, line near the quiver axis); last 2 m at ≤1 m/s with the quiver pitched to the measured line angle; nose probe enters the 120 mm trumpet; the trumpet lip closes the leading edges like an umbrella pulled handle-first through a ring (the reel supplies the ≈5–15 N); nose seats on pogo contacts + 1/2" N52 magnet (detent only); 3–5 N line tension on the ratchet is the primary retention; quiver folds back.

capture_reliability_drivers.note: Illustrative only: every distribution is ASSUMED. The line passes through the mouth eyelet, so position error is self-centred; the drivers are entry angle vs trumpet half-angle, roll at entry (asymmetric spar contact), icing and line wraps. Retries correlate (same wind), so within-3 is optimistic.

notes: Position error at the mouth is self-centring because the line passes through the eyelet; the risk is attitude (entry angle vs 45° trumpet half-angle, roll at entry → asymmetric spar contact), icing of mouth/sail, line wrap after a tumble, and body-wake turbulence in the last metre.
Retry = pay out 1–2 m and re-approach (≈3 s). The towglider audit kill test applies: 50 captures at −10 °C, kill if <95 % first-time.

umbrellaDelta.desc: folding delta (Rogallo-type) with umbrella runner, LE 0.45 m, span 0.75 m

foldGlider.desc: rigid folding glider, span 0.80 m, chord 0.10 m, tail (towglider-class)

comparison.umbrellaDelta: L/D 4.5–6 (ASSUMED polar, flexible sail, camera pod); folds passively in the trumpet; tolerant of capture misalignment; spars 5 mm carbon (calc); medium strike hazard; packs into Ø52 × 0.47 m. CHOSEN.
comparison.foldGlider: L/D ≈10 → lowest launch wind (but elevation then needs even more braking); a rigid wing must be folded by actuators or a cam track during capture; 140 g → KE cap 14.6 m/s; towglider needed 2.8 L just for a holster. Back-up if the delta polar disappoints.
comparison.ramAir: lightest, safest on impact, packs smallest; but collapses at low apparent wind, cannot re-inflate on the line, camera on a bridle pendulum, and a soft canopy is the hardest thing to re-dock automatically (kite2 needed a snuffer). Rejected for auto-dock; keep for a manual-stow variant.

elevationControl.why: un-braked equilibria sit at 70–82° (calc) — top-down framing and head clearance <1 m. Hold 40–55° with tow-point AoA trim (flat-plate branch L/D≈cot α, α 35–50°) or a servo tail drogue.

quiverTube.crushNote: a falling rider (≈800 N) ovalises/crushes it: hinge must break away (≤60 N tip load, except along the line) and fold onto the pack

BOM_totals.costClass: prototype BOM order US$400–700 per set excl. tooling (ASSUMED, no quotes requested)

manufacturability: All primary parts are off-the-shelf classes: FPV/robotics BLDC + FOC driver, 18650 cells, fishing braid, pultruded carbon rods/tubes, magnetic encoders.

Custom: CNC drum + clutch, injection-moulded or SLS PA12 trumpet/runner/hinges, sewn Skytex sail (kite-industry process), strain flexure (machined + bonded gauges — calibration over −20…+20 °C needed).
56 mm thin-wall carbon tube is a roll-wrapped stock size class (ASSUMED availability); fallback: 1.2 mm PA12/PC tube (≈+60 g).
Sealing/icing: IP54 back unit, line entry through a felt/brush wiper; heated trumpet lip optional (+1–2 W).

top_risks.risk: Head clearance vs line elevation: ≥1.0 m only for ε ≤55° with a 0.55 m lumbar exit; overfly at stops/gusts puts the line 0.58 m from the helmet (ε 90°).
top_risks.mitigation: elevation control + retract before overfly; 0.65 m exit; line-angle interlock
top_risks.killTest: tethered dummy rig: line distance to a helmet target over posture/elevation sweeps; kill if the controller cannot keep ε≤55° in 9 m/s gusts

top_risks.risk: Rigid 0.55 m quiver behind the pelvis in a fall / sit-back / tree well: injury and breakage.
top_risks.killTest: drop/fall dummy; kill if breakaway force >60 N or tube intrudes into the seat zone

top_risks.risk: Auto-capture reliability (entry angle, roll, ice, wrap) — illustrative MC: 60 % first try with a fixed quiver vs 96 % when the quiver aligns to the line; all inputs ASSUMED.
top_risks.mitigation: quiver pitch alignment, high-AoA approach, 45° trumpet, tail plug, retry logic
top_risks.killTest: 50 captures at −10 °C on a tow rig; kill if <95 % first time

top_risks.risk: Launch out of the body wake at the 7.4 m/s gate; tailwinds where apparent wind <5 m/s cannot launch at all (same physics that killed towglider tail cases).
top_risks.mitigation: pay-out plunger, reel pumping bursts (≤140 W), honest launch gate
top_risks.killTest: wake survey behind a crouched dummy; launch trials

top_risks.risk: Chairlift: inadvertent launch / line snag on lift = catastrophic; stowed comfort against the backrest.
top_risks.mitigation: two-channel lockout (mechanical pin + software), stowed flush plate

top_risks.risk: Delta polar unknown (L/D 4.5–6 and post-stall elevation control ASSUMED); flexible sail flutter → camera jitter.
top_risks.killTest: tow-car polar; kill if ε cannot be held 40–55° with T ≥1.5 N

top_risks.risk: Cold electro-mechanics: regen into a cold pack, strain-flexure drift, ice in ratchet/clutch, braid freezing to the drum.
top_risks.mitigation: shunt brake, thermistor-gated regen, −20 °C calibration, PU-coated line, wiper

top_risks.risk: Third-party line hazard (laceration, clothesline) remains at ε <45° and near lifts/crowds.
top_risks.mitigation: ε ≥45° most of the time, hi-vis line, radar proximity retract, resort permission

bold_ideas_considered: The dock is the launch rail and the line exit (one rigid member, sized properly) — avoids a separate boom.
Passive capture-fold: the reel's own pull folds the wing in the trumpet (umbrella pulled handle-first through a ring).
Line routed along the hollow hinge axis so deploy/fold never changes line length.
Body-heated battery in the lumbar unit instead of a heater-charged flyer cell; LTO/lithium-ion-capacitor flyer buffer as a later option for cold charging.
The flyer's tail disc is the quiver's snow plug.

handoff_to_others.science_aero: please replace the ASSUMED delta polar (CD0 0.075, k 0.095, CLmax 1.0, post-stall L/D≈cot α) and check whether ε 40–55° can be held with the AoA-trim range; body-wake survey at the quiver mouth.
handoff_to_others.science_control: pay-out speed cap 9 m/s (BEMF), reel-in KE governor formula, tension cap 25 N / clutch 35 N, launch gate 7.4 m/s apparent, two-channel chairlift lockout, retract-before-overfly rule for head clearance.
handoff_to_others.integrator: calc is not simulation-judged; do not count anything here as verification.
